promise: Join a band of crime solvers in Black Marsh and climb from petty thefts and larcenies through murder mysteries to a grand murder finale involving highly important people of the province.
core: Solving crimes the Shadowscales (assassins) and the Night-Reed Chapter (thieves) live by, using classic mystery structures made to fit the lore and the world.
identity: A joinable faction of crime solvers, rival to the Shadowscales and the Night-Reed Chapter. Its name, founding, patrons, headquarters and the lore reason someone would pay for and trust detectives are still to come from a lore pass; not yet written.
beats: Early cases are petty crimes: thefts and larcenies
Cases escalate in series of thefts, larcenies and murder mysteries as rank rises
Rivalry with the Shadowscales and the Night-Reed Chapter runs through the line
Recurring cast and a rival, with clues for the finale seeded along the way
Grand finale: a murder mystery that must involve highly important NPCs of Black Marsh
free: Almost everything is open: the faction's name, founding, patrons, headquarters, ranks, number of cases per rank, the cast, which regions host cases, and the finale's victim and culprit. Fixed by the decision only: escalation by case, a joinable faction, rivalry with the two guilds, a grand finale with important NPCs, grounded in lore and in simple classic mystery structures.
source: docs/decisions/0025-a-detectives-faction.md; story/design/narrative-lines.md; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md (§3 crime and the shadow); story/lore/topics/sithis-nisswo-shadowscales.md

promise: You fight the Owing, a humane native debt-labour custom that drifted into inherited bondage, by proving it and burying its dead, and you pay for each win.
core: Injustice with no villain: correct arithmetic, kind brokers and a ruin that is implicated rather than evil. Burial work and abolition work are the same work.
identity: The Blackrose Chainbreakers, who oppose the Owing (debt labour counted in nushmeekos). The tell is washed-out colour and markings from distance from the Hist. Always give the Owing defenders it has genuinely served.
beats: An Owing correct at every step: four months for a boat, eleven years running (BC01)
The burnt Rose registers and estate ledgers as one class of document (BC02)
Ussa-Rekh's thirty years of forgiveness and the brokerage that now indentures the dock crews (BC03)
The procession of the Argonian dead carried home by name by Grave-Singer Ossu through contested crossings (BC05)
What the Rose Becomes, ending in a unglamorous reform of assessment itself (BC06)
Protected in every end: the archive wing, the confiscation-ledger record class and the Rose heirs as a community
free: Which estate, crossing or dock hosts each case, minor workers and witnesses, ledger contents beyond the stated arithmetic, route of the procession.

promise: Eight strange, standalone encounters, one per Prince plus the unexplained, that feel like intrusions of Oblivion into a Hist-and-Sithis world and leave at least one thing unexplained.
core: Wonder and unease: each Prince's bargain is technically intact and practically ruinous, and the choice is the player's, with Argonians reacting from their own cosmology rather than as followers of the Princes.
beats: Each quest is found by rumour, shrine, book or strange encounter, never a quest board
Each Prince's bargain or curse is literally true and quietly ruinous (door wishes, mask wants, drowned-library price)
The player makes a real choice about which side or hunt to finish (cure, quarantine, expose or let it run; which hunt)
At least one element in each stays unexplained (wonder budget)
Fixed unique artifact rewards, not scaled loot
Horror is found through hospitality, memory or rite rather than only through combat
free: Which settlement or ruin hosts each quest, minor cast names, route and set dressing, which of the eight sit in Milestone 1 (DQ01-DQ04) versus wave 2, and which vanilla artifact mesh is re-skinned as the reward.

promise: You stand up for people the old tribal and Hist order has no place for, and every victory sharpens the question of who a free city is really for.
core: Citizenship, property and plural identity, and the risk that openness turns into rule by wealth.
identity: A civic faction of Lukiul, mixed-city citizens, merchants, workers and reformers seeking civic standing independent of tribe or Hist. Ranks: Petitioner, Advocate, Ward Delegate, charter branch office.
beats: A resident is refused registration because no Hist claims them (LW01), and the lore remedy of the Hissmir trials sharpens rather than solves it
The murdered delegate who was exposing League financiers, with the hate-crime story that suits many groups (LW04)
The traditional ordeal demanded in a mixed court (LW05)
The canal that improves sanitation but cuts a sacred route and displaces households (LW08)
The charter negotiation where prior cases limit credible clauses (LW09)
The finale: plural civic movement, merchant oligarchy, municipal service, or collapse after exposing its own contradictions (LW10)
free: Which city hosts each case, minor people, street and building layouts, route names, market and warehouse dressing, the names of blocs and officials other than the named ones (Advocate Oshu-Kai).
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 38 The League of Open Water; story/lore/topics/hist-and-sap.md; story/lore/regions/shadowfen.md

promise: The province feels lived in: each place has its own problem that comes from its ground, water, history and people, not from a hero's errand.
core: Local trouble is caused by real arrangements (tolls, rites, debts, records, stone and water) and the player settles it by reading them, with choices that favour some people over others.
beats: Every quest starts from a causal local situation (geography, culture, politics, someone's motive) rather than a fetch list.
No quest is only collecting objects; recovery needs ownership, route, danger or interpretation to make it a problem.
The quest-giver is the payload: a person with a local occupation and one stated want.
Each region packet holds at least one oddity with no faction stakes, reward or explanation.
Cross-line texture comes through shared places and networks, never imported characters; delivery stays mostly low-tier (moved evidence, aftermath, retrieval).
free: Which places host which quest, the names of minor people, routes, set dressing and the order of regional packets; skeleton premises may be reshaped as long as the shape of the problem survives.

promise: A debtor the law thinks dead is carried from a burnt work camp to the empty throne and the sanctuary door, and in the end holds the jewel, the city and the outcome, and must choose what to take.
core: Can a people be protected by a bond they are not free to refuse, and when the fight over that bond is done, what do you do with what you are holding? The cult's grievance is real; its severance is indiscriminate.
beats: MQ01: the Owing-gang processing, then the Unbound Root's attack led in person by Cuts-the-Old-Knot, who takes the courier's satchel and decides the player is not worth killing; a Hist turns its face and its egg clutch dies that night
The recurring sap-dreams begin the night of the attack (circle of trees, a door not yet built, a voice) and return at authored beats
MQ05: the arrival walk at Helstrom passes the Hall of the Scalded Throne, empty for centuries and still swept, so the endgame's third option stands in a room in Act I
MQ26: the hidden archive shows the Root of Accord was an ancient voluntary accord converted into a compulsory state instrument
MQ20 and MQ22: the Reed's own sap-dream files and the two incompatible reports, where a lie or truth has a visible victim and the player's handler falls
MQ18: the preacher at the sermon house is the Collector, Opens-the-Last-Door, who knows the player and says nothing

MQ29 to MQ31: the Lost City and its Last Warden, then the door confrontation where a seeded principal stands opposed, with a speech route and a hard fair duel always available, ending in the three families CUT, CLAIM or MEND
free: Which settlement, cell or building hosts a beat; names of minor people; the exact routes, boats and roads; which of the regional leads (MQ07, 09, 10, 13, 14) are used as long as three suffice; set dressing; the exact room for the Scalded Throne; levels and enemy placements (nothing levelled against the player).

promise: You are the one who goes into the danger and finds the truth, then stands in council and decides what it is worth. Every hearing pays off something won underwater, upriver or inside someone's work camp.
core: Consent, stewardship and the limits of traditional authority: no Hist speaks for all Hist, and every remedy benefits some residents at the cost of others.
identity: Tree-Minders and Hist communities mediating ecology, eggs, sap, roads and local autonomy without assuming one voice. Ranks Helper, Root-Walker, Community Mediator, branch Conclave office. Plural and reform branches coexist; hardline closed leadership conflicts with senior Open Water League office.
beats: Discover in danger, decide in council: each quest's evidence is gathered in a dive, boat run, camp infiltration or den before the hearing.
MR01 root-cave dive finds the founders' hand-cut breach; the cure and whether the founders are named are the player's call.
MR02 night boat run with the eggs aboard, adoption terms answered at the far dock, the flood being engineered upstream.
MR04 night entry into the harvest camp with a blown-cover escape; the loudest ban campaigner is the biggest quiet buyer.
MR05 the den in the abandoned grove and the truth that the curer led the clutch out that night.
MR08 the council convened by clearing the channel, the toll and the falsified minutes, then run by one procedure (Ixo-Vaal or Kaska-Meen).
MR10 the loading-dock intercept of a genuine-paper cutting taking, then the finale choice of what the Conclave becomes.
free: Which Hist settlement, grove, channel or dock hosts each quest; names of minor people; exact routes and hazard points; set dressing. The mid-line procedure choice and the end states must stay.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 36 The Many-Root Conclave; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Many-Root; story/lore/topics/hist-and-sap.md; story/lore/topics/hist-placement.md

promise: You take paid, practical defence work in a swamp frontier and discover that who is protected, and who is billed, is the real contract.
core: Professional competence versus exploitation, public service, ecology, and whether accepting a charter means becoming foreign.
identity: A native martial tradition (Four Winds of Stonewastes, shellback levies, kaals, hired village defenders) arguing over accepting a foreign chartered form; explicitly not a Fighters Guild branch. Ranks: Recruit, Proven Blade, Contract Captain, charter branch office.
beats: The first contract understates the danger and overcharges residents (FG01)
Patrol vanished after refusing an unsafe order: negligence, not a monster (FG02)
The juvenile Wamasu: kill, relocate, return eggs or expose trophy hunters (FG03)
Charter War, with Ka-Deelith Ushu's hereditary-defence argument as the hardest to answer and least practical (FG08)
The extermination order that targets a marsh community for its land and water, read aloud by Halvar the Damp before he signs (FG09)
The four outcomes: public service, disciplined mercenary company, An-Xileel auxiliary, broken protection cartel (FG10)
free: Villages, forts and creature habitats used, minor officers, trophy and ledger details, exact routes, which old guild hall is reused.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 33 The Marsh Charter; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md (cited in section 33)

promise: You rise from proving yourself on a small recovery to a province-famous heist on Lilmoth's Crown Ledger, and then decide who owns the night.
core: Skill and loyalty among the dispossessed, professional restraint, criminal mutual aid, and the pull of blackmail power.
identity: A native Argonian thieves guild (not an Imperial franchise) adapted to canals, boats, flooded districts and rootworm routes. Ranks Lookout, Cutpurse, Water-Rat, Night-Reed, senior branch outcome. No Nocturnal oath. Three desks with three ethics: Deep-In-Her-Cups at Soulrest (restraint), Vasha 'Half-Rent' at Lilmoth (leverage), Sails-By-Morning at Archon (velocity).
beats: TG01: prove value by recovering stolen goods without harming the thief, observation and social leverage over burglary
TG02: the drowned lockbox whose contents expose all three clients
TG07: Silt is innocent, is never told she was suspected, and is cleared without alerting the real informer the den trusts too much
TG08 and TG09: the Pusbottom vault as route-planning lesson, and two of four optional preparations, none mandatory
TG10: the Tidal Palace heist with player-chosen methods and the ripper eels turned aside by eel-slime
TG11: the ledger proves patrons, merchants and officials jointly engineered housing seizures, and you expose, sell, redistribute or build an oligarchy
free: Which docks, dens, houses and mooring spots stand in; names of minor people and fences; tool and route details; the Archon fence den location. Palace and vault names may change with the world's own seat of government.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 32; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md section 3; story/lore/topics/ecology-encounters-loot.md section 2; story/design/quests/36-cast-roster.md section 56; story/design/quests/index/factions.md

promise: You learn a living Argonian tradition of death, change and mediation by taking part, and help decide whether it stays dispersed or builds a school.
core: Plural belief, grief, mercy and fraud, and the danger of turning change into dogma. You end as a respected interpreter, not an unquestioned prophet.
identity: A mainstream Argonian Sithis tradition focused on change, death, interpretation and community mediation, distinct from the Unbound Root. Ranks Listener, Path-Bearer, Interpreter, then regional teacher or itinerant elder by outcome.
beats: NI01: a funeral dispute teaches that Nisswo practice is interpretive, not a rigid death cult
NI02: a silent Nisswo takes you through a six-stop day and you err publicly at least twice; she never says what it was for
NI05: the Teeth of Sithis, a violent Sul-Xan splinter, and telling sincere theology from opportunism and state provocation
NI07: the admired priest who invents revelations and also made a real peace
NI08: a condemned murderer, victims and the state, resolved by process, not a pardon or execution binary
NI09 and NI10: dispersed order or teaching house, ending as plural network, formal school, itinerant tradition or dissolved order
free: Which shrines, platforms, homes and settlements are used, names of minor people, routes. The pilgrimage circuit in the authoring nudge is optional, to keep or drop on fit.

promise: A holding bin of unauthored ideas raised by the 2026-09-04 quest and world co-design pass; no promise to the player until an author picks one up.
core: Each proposal is a mystery or dispute grown out of a place in the plotted province (weirs, sluices, crossings, stations, stakes); the bin itself has no theme beyond that.
beats: No beat is binding: none is authored, none has a brief or cast
Any author picking one up must re-run the collision test against the current index first
Any proposal may be dropped without loss
free: Everything: the whole line is unauthored and any row may be dropped, reshaped or merged.

promise: You run the water routes that keep Argonia moving, and decide whether the pilots' trade stays mutual aid or becomes a cartel.
core: Mobility, labour, monopoly and sacred routes, and the line between mutual aid and cartel power.
identity: The Reed-Sail Compact: pilots, ferries, boat crews, smugglers and dock workers. Ranks: Deckhand, Pilot, Route-Keeper, branch-specific officer. Includes a pirate branch (Salt-Teeth arc).
beats: Earning the pole on a working ferry with current, passengers and a staged obstruction, not a combat test (RS01)
Ferry in the Dark: hunted passenger evaded by route and timing past static watcher boats (RS02)
Pirates of Topal: a crew of ferry workers displaced by a monopoly (RS05)
Storm at Archon: allocating limited rescue capacity, with Ahnjazzi's letter read aloud (RS07)
Compact or Cartel: the internal election and which votes stay legitimate (RS09)
Open Channels: worker compact, merchant cartel, pirate confederation or regulated public ferry (RS10)
free: Docks, routes and hubs used, minor pilots and passengers, boat and cargo detail, cove and ship placement; the pirate-branch quests are concept and wave 2.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 37 The Reed-Sail Compact and section 43 Salt-Teeth arc; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md

promise: You serve a small order that keeps the secret root-transit routes running, and decide what the order becomes.
core: Sacred routes and access: mutual aid against monopoly, safety against secrecy. The worm is never seen, only its effects.
identity: A handful of keepers on routes secret by doctrine; two fixed posts: Ki-Ossa at the Helstrom terminus (also the restrictionist voice) and Tuxo at the hidden station. Two desks by declared canon exception.
beats: The worm is never on screen: presence reads through a tunnel mouth, churned water, wake, sound.
RW01 the refusal read entirely from behaviourless evidence.
RW03 a sacred route sold to smugglers to fund repairs the state refused.
RW04 reopen the route by cutting living roots or abandoning a dependent settlement.
RW05 four end states (open public service, restricted sacred order, state bureau, dispersed keepers), all keeping the Helstrom terminus in service.
free: Station positions (the layout is a placeholder awaiting Hist-node placement), pen and cavern layouts, minor handlers, smuggler identities.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 42 Rootworm Waykeepers; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Rootworm Waykeepers; story/lore/topics/roads-and-routes-4e201.md

promise: You are drawn into the contest over reviving an order everyone wants and nobody made, and you decide what the Shadowscales become.
core: Duty, consent and political assassination: whether birth, tradition, state power or consent can recreate a real order, or only a useful costume.
identity: A dead assassin order (training facility shut 4E 187, last known Shadowscale dies 4E 201) with four bidders: Dark Brotherhood, Black-Tongues, the Veiled Reed state, and an independent ethical order. Ranks Watcher, Knife-Bearer, Writ-Keeper, senior branch office; leadership only in the independent branch, answerable to a council.
beats: SS01: the last trained Shadowscale dies in the player's hands and the list of surviving initiates is the prize
SS02: a writ from an authority that does not exist, and each choice states the order's legal philosophy
SS03: the ruined hatchery and a survivor who never consented
SS04, SS05 and SS08: three bidders (Black-Tongues, Brotherhood, Veiled Reed) each offer legitimacy for control
SS07: two knives, one name, where authentic and innocent diverge and executing either claims the empty throne's authority
SS09: the Night Mother ritual with ambiguous evidence and a staged deception
SS10: the final choice among state service, Brotherhood, independent ethical order, or dissolution with records returned to victims
free: Where the ruined facility, hatchery, safehouses, courthouse and meeting rooms sit, names of minor people, rooftop and canal routes, which city fabric is reused. The design says not to build a province-scale assassin network.

promise: You work among scholars and custodians who all want a piece of what lies under the water, and you decide whose knowledge it is and what gets published.
core: Ownership of knowledge, research ethics, translation, and the political force of archives, with the fight over whether such a body should become an institution at all.
identity: Black Marsh scholars between local custodians, the Synod and the College of Whispers after the Mages Guild's fall. Not robed mages: tree-minders, alchemists, grave-singers, jekka-wats, bone-workers and a few foreign-trained scholars. Spine is the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold. Ranks Copyist, Field Reader, Custodian, branch-aligned senior scholar. Synod, College and independent endings are mutually exclusive.
beats: SA01 recovering a waterproofed text from an inhabited ruin whose owners are present.
SA04 the College's offer of independence hiding a binding experiment and the exhumation of Umbriel's dead.
SA05 the Synod's funding against exclusive custody, with Hierem the Synod grandee in the archive's own records.
SA08 reading an escaped construct's wake at fixed breach points and choosing which containment point to hold.
SA09 Three Charters: Synod, College and independent futures are incompatible and earlier conduct changes support.
SA10 What We Publish: open archive, local custody, Imperial institution or suppression.
free: Which ruins, camps and offices host each quest; names of minor scholars; the choice of creature or construct; routes. Staffing must stay non-robed and local.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 34 The Sunken Archive; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Sunken Archive; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md sections 1-2

promise: You help Argonian and Dunmer neighbours contain border violence without erasing slavery, invasion or living claims.
core: Competing memory and present economics: the hardest question (saltrice title) cuts across the ethnic line, not along it.
identity: The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord: Argonian and Dunmer residents of Thorn trying to contain border violence; both militias are the wrong shape for the real problems.
beats: One memorial site, two commemorated atrocities (TA01)
A body on the ferry: the victim moved Owing-held labourers as freight, ending in a manhunt via ferries and static intercepts (TA02)
Saltrice fields with no titles, only occupation, worked under Owings by an ex-Archein family (TA03)
Both militias keep lists of civilians to seize (TA04)
Ash-Reed Accord: truth commission, security pact, closed separation or factional victory (TA05)
free: Neighbourhoods, field and dock locations, minor suspects and family names, militia room layouts.

promise: You handle an inherited catastrophe that nobody alive saw, and decide how the truth of Umbriel is kept, told or buried.
core: History argued over at the distance of inherited memory: edited testimony, missing households, and a Society whose own founding account is compromised.
identity: Inheritors and archivists, not survivors. Desks: Keeps-The-Count at the Lilmoth archive room, Neexa-Tul behind a Pusbottom chandlery (the dead belong to families; testimony may be consulted, never kept; write one line of your own family's before reading), and Old Nusa at Deepmire.
beats: UW01 two witness texts, one edited after its author's death.
UW03 a household omitted from every casualty list.
UW04 the expedition to the Refuge at Deepmire, Old Nusa who is bored of Umbriel, and proof the Society's founding testimony came from a collaborator of Hierem's agents.
UW05 the choice of full archive, protected testimony, official narrative or sealed evidence, now including the Society itself.
free: Archive, home and workshop locations; names of minor people; the route and shelters of the UW04 trek, provided it remains the line's one traversal spike.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 41 Umbriel Witness Society; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Umbriel Witness; story/lore/topics/umbriel.md; story/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md section 9

spirit: A boat-damage Owing of four nushmeekos has run eleven years and the arithmetic is correct at every step.
must_keep: Never-Sold proves the arithmetic in front of the man who did it, which does not free her, because arithmetic is not the problem.
free: Estate and worker.
needs: Ex-Archein estate quarters, ledger office, toll crossing, multi-page checkable account.

spirit: The Rose's burnt registers and the estate ledgers are the same class of document and reading them finds people still held.
must_keep: The archive wing survives every outcome; the reading decides whose legitimacy survives.
free: Which family.
needs: Burnt archive wing, duplicate records, estate ledgers, descendant contacts.

spirit: Ussa-Rekh forgave debts for thirty years and built the brokerage that now indentures the Soulrest and Archon dock crews.
must_keep: He keeps every forgiven ledger and can name the year it turned.
free: Home details.
needs: Broker home, hiring office, safehouse, hearing room.

spirit: Factions inside the Rose prepare an uprising with incompatible aims, and preventing it keeps an abusive hierarchy that feeds four hundred.
must_keep: Prevention preserves the hierarchy; violence can be met as aftermath.
free: Yard layout.
needs: The Rose yard, cell blocks, armory, medical room; actor cap 6.

spirit: Grave-Singer Ossu carries the Argonian dead of White Rose Prison home by name past hostile crossings.
must_keep: The procession and the argument at each crossing.
free: Route.
needs: White Rose ruin, bone-store cells, procession route with tolls, burial ground.

spirit: Finale: recognise the Rose, disperse it as a hierarchy only, raise a memorial over the undead levels, or reform assessment itself.
must_keep: Four ends, heirs, archive wing and ledger record class always survive; the assessment reform is local to Gideon's courthouse.
free: Notices.
needs: Rose variants, Gideon courthouse.

spirit: A remote village venerates the memory of the Knahaten Flu as a cleansing while a Peryite cultist works to make it literal. The afflicted disagree about being saved.
must_keep: The village honestly reveres the Flu, the cultist wants it real, and the player picks cure, quarantine, expose or let it run.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 2-3. A remote, shut community of houses with a shrine or apparatus place, sick and healthy villagers, plague effects from vanilla, a hidden cultist.

spirit: A drowned Xanmeer library gives any answer wanted, including main-quest and faction secrets, for a memory the game really removes.
must_keep: The answer costs a memory that is actually removed, and essential material is never offered.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 3. A drowned Xanmeer interior reachable by water or diving, with strange Apocrypha audio and visual effects.

spirit: Hunters pursue a great marsh beast while Hircine has marked the least honourable of them as prey.
must_keep: The hunters are the prey and the player chooses which hunt ends.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 3-4. Open marsh ground with a great beast, a hunters' camp, and room for an ambush of the hunters.

spirit: A sealed plantation door grants wishes to whoever feeds it deeds of ownership, and every wish is technically intact and practically ruinous.
must_keep: The wish goes to whoever feeds the door a deed, and it comes out ruinous.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 2. A plantation estate with one sealed door, a few residents ruined by past wishes, and papers and deeds to find or forge.

spirit: A Shadowscale cowl that erases its wearer from memory is in use by someone the whole village has forgotten.
must_keep: The wearer is someone the village cannot remember and the player must rebuild them.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 2-3. A small village with homes to search, villagers who share a gap in memory, and traces left by a forgotten person.

spirit: A hospitable stilt-house inn on a route never lacks meat, and the horror is found through hospitality, not combat.
must_keep: The meat's source is found through hospitality and guests defend their hosts.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 2. A stilt-house inn with guest rooms, a kitchen and stores, a handful of guests and hosts; reuses the inn layout of LQ28.

spirit: Meridia's agent demands the end of a beloved funerary practice that technically produces undead, which mourners treat as their dead visiting at floodtide.
must_keep: Meridia's agent wants the rite destroyed and both sides are sincere.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 2-3. A necropolis village with preserved dead, floodtide, a funerary rite place, mourners and Meridia's agent; vanilla draugr re-dressed.

spirit: A pre-Duskfall mask lets its wearer hear what everyone in a room privately wants and slowly replaces those wants with the wearer's own.
must_keep: The mask's reading of wants is real and its corruption stays unsaid.
free: Settlement, minor cast names, set dressing and the exact reward item; the Prince's bargain stays.
needs: Danger 3. A tactile ruin holding the mask, and a room of people to read with it.

spirit: A routine defence contract proves the employer understated the danger and overcharged residents.
must_keep: The discovery of the understated danger and overcharge.
free: Village, employer.
needs: A palisaded village, creature approach lanes, contract office.

spirit: A patrol vanished after refusing an unsafe order; the evidence reads as negligence, not a monster.
must_keep: Evidence that the officer was at fault.
free: Route, survivors.
needs: Marsh patrol route, evidence trail, survivor shelter, small predator ground. Danger low.

spirit: A juvenile Wamasu threatens farms because hunters killed its prey and stole its eggs.
must_keep: Options: kill, relocate, return eggs, or expose trophy hunters.
free: Farm, nest site, hunters.
needs: Wetland territory, nest, farm edge, boat access, large creature arena. A big wetland predator (design flags a creature substitution question).

spirit: The guild billed several villages for the same slain creature using forged trophies and staged attacks. Wave 2.
must_keep: Uncovering the forged trophies and double billing.
free: Villages involved.
needs: Records room, tax office, trophy store, two villages.

spirit: Two communities paid for the same fort restoration and both expect protection, but the commander will abandon the poorer one.
must_keep: Who the fort protects.
free: Which two settlements.
needs: A reusable frontier fort with two approaches, barracks, council scenes.

spirit: A disease-transformed Argonian keeps reason intermittently, and the village argues cure, containment or execution.
must_keep: Cure versus containment versus execution.
free: Village, healer.
needs: Quarantine hut, healer space, victim homes, secure room.

spirit: Local officers encourage bandits to keep villages dependent on charter contracts.
must_keep: Expose, seize or redirect the racket.
free: Camp location, village.
needs: Roadside bandit camp, office, village, ambush route.

spirit: Reformers, mercenary captains and the Four Winds compete over what the Charter is for.
must_keep: Ka-Deelith Ushu's argument that hereditary unpaid defence is the only kind that lasts; skill and conduct decide who follows you.
free: Hall layouts, banners.
needs: Guildhall meeting floor, training yard, records archive, the Four Winds hall at Stonewastes. No city battle.

spirit: A lucrative extermination order targets a marsh community that never asked for help; the real client wants their land and water.
must_keep: The unsolicited order read aloud by Halvar the Damp before he signs, and the choice of how to meet the community.
free: Community, client estate.
needs: Remote marsh community, disputed resource site, client estate, hostile and non-hostile encounter setups.

spirit: Finale: the charter becomes public service, mercenary company, An-Xileel auxiliary or broken cartel.
must_keep: The four outcomes, with rank tied to martial competence and decisions.
free: Banners, notices.

free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. a body, a scene and a small set of suspects; one strange, unexplained thing in a setting that suits it.

spirit: The bundle at the bottom of the rack has been rewrapped four times. No carrier will take it the last stage home.
must_keep: No carrier will take it the last stage home.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. a rite, its ritual place and the people who keep it; an heir or successor and a household with something to inherit.

spirit: A deliberate hand is pulling grave-stakes. The stakes taken so far form a pattern.
must_keep: The stakes taken so far form a pattern.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. a past act that can be traced and answered for; a haunted place with spirits or undead and its history. Set in hist-heartland, near necropolis dead tenders.

spirit: One gatehouse on a two-toll bridge has issued the other gatehouse's receipts for nine years.
must_keep: One gatehouse on a two-toll bridge has issued the other gatehouse's receipts for nine years.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Cut, not to be built: absorbed by LD47 (same bridge, same fraud reversal). Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. marks, grave-stakes or tokens and an elder or witness who can read them; two rival parties with a standing claim to the same thing. Set in dunmer-north, near nine fords.

spirit: Two calcinator courts are laid out to a moonless sky. The work done in them fails under any other light.
must_keep: The work done in them fails under any other light.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. one strange, unexplained thing in a setting that suits it; two or more parties who will talk, in a place where they can meet.

spirit: The province's working sky-calendar has one hereditary keeper. The keeper has no successor. The office has a recorded power over the weather.
must_keep: The keeper has no successor. The office has a recorded power over the weather.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. one strange, unexplained thing in a setting that suits it; an heir or successor and a household with something to inherit.

spirit: Unattended sluices still open and close on the season. Four villages set their planting by the sluices. No owner of the machine is recorded.
must_keep: Four villages set their planting by the sluices. No owner of the machine is recorded.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. one strange, unexplained thing in a setting that suits it; two rival parties with a standing claim to the same thing. Set in a deep-delta Hist-tribe setting, near naga village settled.

spirit: An Imperial roadworks stopped mid-formation centuries ago. Something is still drawing against the roadworks' account.
must_keep: Something is still drawing against the roadworks' account.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. marks, grave-stakes or tokens and an elder or witness who can read them; a past act that can be traced and answered for.

spirit: The Flu cordon's ration ledgers are still in the store. The ledgers record which households received rations. Blackrose has not opened the ledgers since.
must_keep: The ledgers record which households received rations. Blackrose has not opened the ledgers since.
free: Everything: no brief or cast exists; the premise is a seed and may be reshaped or dropped.
needs: Proposed and unauthored, danger not stated. a past act that can be traced and answered for; fouled water or sickness and its source. Set in imperial-penal-south, near flu quarantine village.

spirit: Qualify as a pilot by running a real ferry route.
must_keep: A skill test of current, passengers and a staged obstruction, not combat.
free: Route, passengers.
needs: Ferry corridor with two docks and a current.

spirit: Carry a hunted person at night past law and criminals.
must_keep: Choosing route, concealment and whether to ask why; evading fixed watcher boats, not a chase.
free: Landings, hiding pocket.
needs: Night boat corridor, alternate landing, reed hiding spot, 2-3 moored watcher boats.

spirit: A sealed crate holds a living creature trafficked for alchemy.
must_keep: Releasing it risks passengers and ecology.
free: Creature kind, buyer.
needs: Cargo boat, warehouse, alchemist site, release habitat.

spirit: A toll station sinks financially as guards and pilots run a private tariff.
must_keep: Reform or capture the toll.
free: Station details.
needs: Toll station, office, dock, ledgers, patrol schedules.

spirit: A pirate crew includes ferry workers displaced by a monopoly.
must_keep: Boarding, negotiation, sabotage and rescue all stay viable; the crew is reused by ST01.
free: Cove, ship.
needs: Coastal route, pirate cove and ship, boarding arena, hidden landing. Danger moderate.

spirit: Veteran pilots give wrong directions to resist a map registry that would expose sacred routes.
must_keep: Resistance for sacred routes against a registry.
free: Sites. Wave 2.
needs: Pilot guildhouse, map office, three route markers.

spirit: A storm traps ships outside Archon and you allocate limited rescue among passenger, cargo and military vessels.
must_keep: The allocation, with Ahnjazzi's correspondent reading her manifest-pricing letter over the wind.
free: Hull details.
needs: Archon harbour, 3 fixed grounded craft, storm water, timer, rescue markers.

spirit: A merchant coalition proposes a chain across the river and a monopoly checkpoint, promising safety at the cost of free movement. Wave 2.
must_keep: Safety versus free movement.
free: Which river chokepoint.
needs: River chokepoint, chain asset, fort or toll office, alternate shallow channel.

spirit: Violence forces an internal Compact election.
must_keep: Your methods decide which votes stay legitimate.
free: Hall, blocs.
needs: Compact hall, dock assembly, private rooms.

spirit: Finale: worker compact, merchant cartel, pirate confederation or regulated public ferry.
must_keep: The four outcomes.
free: Banners, schedules.
needs: Dock and boat service variants across 3-4 hubs.

spirit: A rootworm refuses a familiar route and handlers disagree on the cause.
must_keep: The cause read wholly from behaviourless evidence; no worm on screen.
free: Station and evidence places.
needs: A rootworm station with a service cavern, refusal-evidence sites and an alternate destination.

spirit: A wanted traveller asks transit under an obsolete sanctuary custom.
must_keep: The custom invoked and the decision whether to carry them.
free: Hall, records.
needs: A waiting hall, a private pen read as occupied by water and sound, records, exits.

spirit: A Waykeeper sells a sacred route to smugglers to fund repairs the state refused.
must_keep: The sale and its purpose; the keeper's reason.
free: Station, cache.
needs: A hidden station, a smuggler cache, a damaged route chamber.

spirit: A route can reopen only by cutting living roots or abandoning a dependent settlement.
must_keep: The two-cost choice.
free: Settlement and ferry.
needs: A blocked root tunnel, a settlement, an alternate ferry route; two local states.

spirit: The order chooses what it becomes: open service, sacred order, state bureau or dispersed keepers.
must_keep: All four end states keep the Helstrom terminus in service.
free: Station schedules.
needs: Station service variants across three nodes, including Helstrom.

spirit: Recover a waterproofed text from an inhabited submerged ruin without taking it from its owners.
must_keep: Local ownership respected; the translation reveals a method, not treasure.
free: Which ruin, which family.
needs: A submerged shrine or house with air pockets, a custodian's home, social and dive routes.

spirit: A scholar's method uses volunteered Hist-memory fragments, and consent cannot be proven after translation.
must_keep: The player audits the method and the affected participant.
free: Lab and pool layout.
needs: An archive laboratory, interview room, ritual pool.

spirit: An untranslated tablet makes a modern family heirs of an ancient office, and three parties want different readings.
must_keep: The tablet's reading and the rival claimants.
free: Family, hearing place.
needs: A tablet display, a family home, a hearing room; Stormhold area.

spirit: College envoys offer independence while hiding a binding experiment and the exhumation of Umbriel's dead.
must_keep: The hidden experiment and the desecration the College calls research.
free: Guest lab and envoys.
needs: A guest laboratory, containment room, small magical encounter space.

spirit: The Synod offers money and instruments in return for exclusive custody of discoveries.
must_keep: The custody demand and the archive's counter-argument that Hierem was a Synod grandee.
free: Office and cellar.
needs: A Synod office, a secure cellar, a negotiation scene.

spirit: A murdered researcher's notes are rebuilt from field sites, and the killer was shielding a community.
must_keep: Rebuild from two of three proofs; the killer's reason, a real unethical experiment.
free: Camps, community.
needs: Two small field camps, a scholar's room, a victim community.

spirit: An excavated Xanmeer is both a sacred site and a village's quarry.
must_keep: Preservation, continued use and research all carry real costs.
free: Village and dig.
needs: An excavated ruin beside a village with quarry, shrine and scholar camp; access states.

spirit: A construct has already passed through the waterways; the player reads its wake and picks where to hold.
must_keep: Read the damage at fixed breach points and choose a containment point, right or costlier; destroy, capture or prove which institution caused it.
free: Breach sites, creature type.
needs: A laboratory breach, three or four breach sites with readable damage, two containment endpoints, a creature; no pursuit.

spirit: Synod, College and independent scholars offer incompatible futures, shaped by earlier conduct.
must_keep: The three-way institutional choice.
free: Hall and offices.
needs: An archive council hall with three offices.

spirit: A discovery could delegitimise land claims and expose sacred information; you choose its publication.
must_keep: Open archive, controlled local custody, Imperial institution or secret suppression.
free: City reactions.
needs: Archive final-state variants and reaction places.

spirit: A dying contract-killer claims to be the last trained Shadowscale and asks you to recover the list of surviving initiates before the An-Xileel or Brotherhood does.
must_keep: The last Shadowscale's death and the hunt for the initiates list.
free: Exact site; the natural site is the sealed Archon training facility but any ruin works. Ambush shape.
needs: A ruined safehouse or sealed facility with a sickroom, hidden archive, two entrances and room for one small ambush. Danger low.

spirit: The first test is a historical writ whose issuing authority no longer exists, and may never have. You decide how to treat it.
must_keep: Executing, investigating, exposing or voiding the writ each sets the order's legal philosophy, with a non-lethal resolution available.
free: Target, route, which rooftop or underwater approach.
needs: A target's home and work route, a public records office, rooftop and underwater approaches, witnesses.

spirit: A ruined hatchery looks abandoned, but records show the children were redirected into state service after the old order fell. One survivor denies ever consenting.
must_keep: The survivor who never consented and the records of redirection.
free: Which ruin, trap layout, memory props. No child NPCs are needed.
needs: A ruined hatchery dungeon with nursery, training yard, flooded archive and traps. Danger moderate.

spirit: Rival revivalists, including the Black-Tongues who quietly kept Shadow-born, claim an adult for his birth sign. He just wants to go on building boats.
must_keep: The claimant's birth sign does not settle his wishes, fitness or obligations.
free: Meeting spaces, the claimant's home and trade details.
needs: Two faction meeting spaces, a neutral hearing room, the claimant's home and a small duel arena.

spirit: A Dark Brotherhood emissary offers training, contracts and Listener legitimacy, but the price is absorption of the order.
must_keep: A courteous, useful offer whose plain aim is control.
free: Safehouse and dock details, the emissary's name.
needs: A guest safehouse, a ritual chamber, a discreet dock or escape route, room for four-person negotiation.

spirit: A contract names a corrupt magistrate, but the patron is a smuggler erasing a conviction.
must_keep: Discovery and restraint are rewarded over any one prescribed kill method.
free: Town, magistrate, smuggler, approach (poison, stealth, social).
needs: A courthouse or magistrate's home, a smuggler warehouse, patrols, space for several approaches. Imperial-fringe town.

spirit: Two assassins use one Shadowscale title; one is an impostor, the other committed an atrocity under a genuine writ. Authenticity and innocence diverge.
must_keep: Executing either claims the empty throne's authority, because a Shadowscale may not kill a Shadowscale. Pursuit is by inference across three vacated sites.
free: Site locations, the two assassins' names.
needs: Twin safehouses, three vacated sites read by evidence, an interrogation room. No fleeing-NPC pathing.

spirit: The Veiled Reed offers a state charter giving protection and resources for state-directed contracts. Refusal leaves the order vulnerable but independent.
must_keep: The third bidder's offer and the choice to refuse it, with no coupling to main-quest trust.
free: Office and council chamber placement.
needs: An An-Xileel office and a Shadowscale council chamber.

spirit: A rite meant to reach the Night Mother yields ambiguous evidence and a staged deception.
must_keep: Three outcomes: bind the order to the Brotherhood, expose the fraud, or adopt a local non-mystical charter.
free: Sanctuary location, lighting and acoustic dressing.
needs: A ritual sanctuary with a coffin or crypt, a secret observer route and one compact combat space.

spirit: The surviving claimants force a final choice that decides what the order becomes.
must_keep: Four ends: state service, Brotherhood affiliation, independent ethical order, or dissolution with records returned to victims.
free: Headquarters location, letters, board dressing.
needs: One headquarters able to show four end states, with NPC schedule swaps and contract boards.

spirit: Pirate branch: a crew has had its flag stolen, and it is the RS05 crew.
must_keep: Link to the RS05 crew; unlocked by the outlaw path. Concept only.
free: Everything beyond the premise.
needs: Coastal waters and a pirate base.

spirit: Pirate branch: a cleanly taken prize carries passengers home and its owner declines to claim the cargo.
must_keep: The decline to claim. Concept only.
free: Everything beyond the premise.
needs: Ships and a port.

spirit: Pirate branch: the Compact holds an election and a mud bank at low tide decides who leads the crew in.
must_keep: Its outcome decides who leads the crew into RS09 and RS10. Concept only.
free: Everything beyond the premise.
needs: Tidal mud bank, ship.

spirit: Standalone Soulrest quest: a pirate confederation opens talks with Soulrest and needs a go-between neither side distrusts.
must_keep: Works without pirate membership; gives non-pirate players the premise. Concept only.
free: Everything beyond the premise.
needs: Soulrest harbour.

spirit: Two communities commemorate different atrocities at one site.
must_keep: Two dates at one memorial.
free: Square details.
needs: Thorn memorial square, archive, family homes.

spirit: A murder looks political but the victim moved Owing-held labourers as freight.
must_keep: The manhunt by ferry network and tide to static intercepts, with capture, kill or bargained escape.
free: Suspects, landings.
needs: Ferry, dock, morgue, two suspect neighbourhoods, two intercept landings on border channels.

spirit: Saltrice fields held by occupation not title, worked under Owings by an ex-Archein family.
must_keep: Force a title, force an audit, broker a division or let it stand; the ledger ignores ancestry.
free: Fields, names.
needs: Saltrice fields, drying floor, counting house, quarters with washed-out workers, a long-unwalked boundary.

spirit: Both militias keep lists of civilians to seize if fighting starts.
must_keep: The two lists.
free: Rooms, routes.
needs: Two militia rooms, safehouse routes, evacuation spots.

spirit: Finale: truth commission, security pact, closed separation or factional victory.
must_keep: The four outcomes.
free: Notices, schedules.
needs: Thorn council and guard variants.

spirit: Prove your value by recovering property one thief took from another, without harming the thief.
must_keep: No harm to the thief; observation and social leverage beat plain burglary.
free: Den, house, property.
needs: A dockside tavern with back rooms, roof and canal exit, plus a small target house with three approaches. Danger low.

spirit: Three clients claim a lockbox in a recently sunk counting house, and its contents show none told the whole truth.
must_keep: The sunk counting house and the contents exposing all three clients.
free: Which building sank, the clients' names.
needs: A submerged counting house with an air pocket, a street entrance and an underwater escape. Water required.

spirit: Customs officers run an illegal tariff while a smuggler uses the scandal to move captives.
must_keep: Three options: steal the tariff ledger, expose both, or take over the route.
free: Town, officers, route.
needs: A customs house, a holding cellar, dock patrols and a boat route. Imperial-fringe coast.

spirit: A wealthy household moves between moorings, so the burglary is a navigation and timing puzzle with optional social entry and hull access.
must_keep: The timing puzzle on a moved houseboat, with optional underwater hull entry.
free: Which household and flotilla; the staged moorings.
needs: A houseboat at three static moorings with deck, interior and hull entrances and actor schedules. Water required.

spirit: Candidate fences in three ports compete, and you judge reliability and hidden loyalties, not quotas.
must_keep: Investigating reliability, not delivering quotas.
free: The three ports and shops.
needs: Three small shops with safe rooms in three port towns.

spirit: The guild plans to intercept a sealed state packet in rootworm transit by impersonation, diversion, bribing Waykeepers or stealing after arrival.
must_keep: The intercept choices around a rootworm transit; the worm never appears.
free: Station pair and tunnel details.
needs: A transit station with service tunnel, waiting area and a sealed packet, reachable by scheduled boat. Hist heartland.

spirit: Someone is selling guild routes and all evidence points at Silt, the young climber, who is innocent.
must_keep: Silt is never told she was suspected; the real informer is someone the den trusts too much.
free: Suspect homes, perches.
needs: Den subrooms, three suspect homes, surveillance perches and a staged accusation scene.

spirit: A flooded municipal vault is a first heist that teaches route planning.
must_keep: Four ways in (roof, sewer, cistern, forged order) converging on one vault, with a no-kill bonus.
free: Vault site and entrances.
needs: A flooded vault in Lilmoth with four entrances, patrols, locks and water.

spirit: Choose two of four preparations (inside schedule, breathing charm, forged seal, portable counterweight), each opening an optional route.
must_keep: Two of four, none a mandatory fetch chain; the direct hard heist stays possible.
free: The four preparation sites.
needs: Four compact preparation locations already part of the city.

spirit: The Crown Ledger heist crosses reception rooms, roofs, service canals, sewers, a cistern and a guarded archive.
must_keep: Player-chosen methods and ripper eels that ignore anyone rubbed with eel-slime; 60 to 90 minutes.
free: Palace layout, disguises.
needs: A large multi-route heist complex in Lilmoth with patrols, canal eel hazard, treasury, vault and boat escape. Water required, danger high.

spirit: The ledger proves patrons, merchants and officials jointly engineered housing seizures, and you decide its fate.
must_keep: Four ends: expose it, sell it, redistribute wealth, or build a disciplined criminal oligarchy.
free: Hall dressing, epilogue notices.
needs: A shared guild hall showing four end states.

spirit: Two witness accounts contradict because one was edited after the author died.
must_keep: The edited text and who changed it.
free: Archive, home, workshop.
needs: An archive, a family home, a scribe workshop.

spirit: A recovered sap sample is evidence, relic and hazard at once.
must_keep: All three readings held against each other.
free: Lab, shrine, debate room.
needs: A secure archive lab, a shrine, a debate room.

spirit: A household vanished from every official casualty list; the player finds it.
must_keep: The omission and the submerged dwelling; descendants told.
free: Dwelling and records place.
needs: A submerged dwelling, municipal records, a descendant's home; Sunkfoot area.

spirit: The real Umbriel memorial is the cursed Refuge at Deepmire, tended by a few caretakers.
must_keep: The D4 expedition, bored Old Nusa, and proof the Society's founding testimony came from a collaborator.
free: Route details, camp.
needs: A plateau approach through bone-country terrain with shelters, a memorial ground, caretaker camp, document cache; danger 4.

spirit: The final choice of how the record is kept: archive, protected testimony, official narrative or sealed.
must_keep: The four outcomes, with the Society itself now at stake.
free: Museum and rumour variants.
needs: Archive and museum state variants and city rumour pools.
